correctness.rationale: Write D=n−1+a+b. With k ones, the up and down transitions share factor (1−ℓ)(2r−1)/(nD), multiplying (n−k)(k+a+t) and k(n−k+b+t) respectively, with t=(1−r)D/(2r−1). Detailed balance gives the stated beta-binomial law. Positive committed weights ensure irreducibility of the labeled chain, so permutation invariance identifies the full exchangeable Bernoulli mixture, even for nonanonymous F. Folding P about 1/2 gives a strictly decreasing likelihood ratio in z when t increases. The sign odds conditional on z do not depend on t: the tilt (1/4−z²)^t cancels. For the Bernoulli response g, a pivotal edge has positive probability under the shared-uniform coupling at any two distinct interior probabilities, so g is strictly increasing; self-duality makes g(1/2+z)−1/2 positive and antisymmetric under reflection. The conditional signed response is therefore strictly increasing in z for a>b, strictly decreasing for a<b, and zero for equality. The order reverses when changing from t to r, including t=0 at r=1; beta concentration as t→∞ gives the fair endpoint. In the illustration the Beta(c+1,c) density is 2p times Beta(c,c); integration by parts using the stated binomial-tail derivative verifies the formula for all m≥0. The weighted-majority example is read within the explicit monotonicity hypothesis: with positive voting weights any self-dual tie resolution is monotone; if zero weights are allowed, monotonicity of the tie resolution must still be imposed. Frozen finite rational tests were inspected as evidence, not executed or relied on for the infinite quantifiers.

originality.rationale: The supported distinct claim is the strict finite-electorate cross-conformity order simultaneously for all coordinatewise monotone self-dual binary rules. The beta-binomial equilibrium and previously known majority comparisons are not novelty claims. A general prior folded-beta likelihood-ratio criterion may cover the folded-magnitude lemma but the available evidence does not give the signed aggregation order.
residual_risks: The folded-beta criterion could cover the magnitude lemma; full theorem text was not obtained. The originality pass is for the signed stationary rule comparison, not for the folded-order lemma in isolation.

value.rationale: This answers a fixed-electorate parameter question not settled by the stationary law, a majority comparison, or a population limit. One strict sign applies to every neutral monotone binary rule, including nonanonymous ones, and identifies the precise role of the exogenous bias. The sign/magnitude decomposition supplies an explanation for that uniformity, with no empirical or finite-time claim.
